    AI Overview
    On April 2, 2026, President Donald Trump fired U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi after a 14-month tenure, primarily due to frustrations regarding her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files and a perceived lack of success in prosecuting the president's political opponents
    . 
    According to reports, the key reasons for her dismissal included: 
    • Handling of Epstein Files: Bondi faced mounting criticism and internal scrutiny over her management of the Department of Justice's (DOJ) release of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
    • Lack of Prosecutions: Trump was reportedly unhappy that Bondi had not acted aggressively enough to investigate or prosecute his political adversaries, such as former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James.
    • Political Pressure: Critics argued her term was defined by attempting to turn the DOJ into a tool for political vendettas, yet she failed to meet the high demands of the White House to secure convictions against critics.
    • Internal Friction: Key outside advisors to Trump, such as Boris Epshteyn and federal housing official Bill Pulte, reportedly pushed for her removal, blaming her for "slow-walking" cases against political enemies. 
    Despite being considered a loyalist who frequently defended the president, these factors, combined with a contentious, "stormy" tenure, led to her ousting.

    AI Overview
    As of March 2026, Pam Bondi is the
    U.S. Attorney General, confirmed following her role as a key ally to Donald Trump, lobbyist, and former Florida Attorney General (2011–2019). She has focused on anti-human trafficking efforts, defending Trump in impeachment proceedings, litigating conservative policies with the America First Policy Institute, and supporting 2020 election challenges. 
    Key actions and roles include: 
    • U.S. Attorney General (2025–Present): Confirmed to the position, she has been involved in overseeing prosecutions of political adversaries and restructuring DOJ staff.
    • Florida Attorney General (2011–2019): Served as Florida’s first female Attorney General, focusing on cracking down on "pill mills" and combating human trafficking.
    • Trump Ally and Defense:
      Served on President Trump’s legal defense team during his first impeachment trial and worked as a special advisor.
    • Lobbyist and Legal Counsel: Worked for Ballard Partners, representing various corporate and foreign interests, including the Qatari government.
    • America First Policy Institute (AFPI): Led litigation efforts at the pro-Trump think tank, targeting voting rights and other policies.
    • Election Challenges: Was involved in questioning the 2020 election results, according to Common Cause. 
    Bondi is a former prosecutor and native of Tampa, Florida.
